newsitem.title: ITALY: IRI to speed up sale of BancaRoma stake.
newsitem.headline: IRI to speed up sale of BancaRoma stake.

text.p: Italian state industrial holding IRI intends to speed up procedures to sell off its holding in Banca di Roma, IRI chairman Gian Maria Gros-Pietro said.
IRI directly holds a stake of 13.8 percent in Banca di Roma as well as 35 percent in Cassa di Risparmio di Roma (CariRoma) holding which controls the bank.

Gros-Pietro said in the text of an address to the lower house Senate industry commission, "During this year...there will be the conclusion or further decisive developments in the sell-off procedures for Autostrade, Aeroporti di Roma Banca di Roma, and Finmare".
Gros-Pietro said that in the period from 1992 to May this year IRI and its sector holdings had carried out privatisation operations for a total value of over 25 trillion lire.
This figure, he said, did not include the divestment of telecoms holding Stet to the Treasury for an overall book value of 18.4 trillion lire.
Once the operations actually underway are completed, IRI's privatisation programme will proceed and be concluded in the next three years according the government's mandate, he said.

"Given this scenario it will be necessary to tighten up the process of overhauling and restructuring the air transport sector and the sectors in which (engineering and defence group) Finmeccanica is active," he added.

Gros-Pietro, appointed new IRI chairman by the Treasury last month, has already said that parts of the sprawling group, like loss-making airline Alitalia, would need serious work before they could be put on the market.
